newsitem.title: BRAZIL: China seeks agricultural cooperation with Brazil.
newsitem.headline: China seeks agricultural cooperation with Brazil.

text.p: Chinese Premier Li Peng visited Brazil's agricultural research center on Saturday seeking more cooperation between the two countries on agriculture projects, including biotechnology.
Li toured the agricultural research agency Embrapa and met with Agriculture Minister Arlindo Porto on his second day in South America's largest country.
An Embrapa statement said China and Brazil wanted to conduct biotechnology projects and exchange data on genetic materials for vegetables, reforestation, soya and pig farming.
Chinese officials also showed an interest in equipment to dry fruit and fish developed at Embrapa, the statement said.

Li, who met President Fernando Henrique Cardoso on Friday, criticized protectionist measures adopted by Brazil, including quotas on textiles, punitive tariffs on toys and a 288 percent tariff on pencil imports.

"It is necessary to improve trade on an equal basis and with reciprocal benefits," the Jornal do Brasil newspaper quoted him telling a group of local journalists. "China does not approve of these protectionist measures."
Li said China had introduced measures facilitating the entry of foreign goods, adding that import tariffs had been reduced in April to 23 percent from 38.9 percent.
He said trade between the two countries, which totalled $2.243 billion in 1995, was too little and should increase.

Li and Cardoso presided over the signing of agreements on satellite cooperation and the environment, and an accord that allows Brazil to maintain its consulate in Hong Kong after the British colony is handed back to Beijing next July 1.

The Chinese leader was due to fly next to Sao Paulo, where he will visit Brazil's space agency on Sunday. Li will visit the Amazon on Monday and fly to Venezuela on Tuesday for the last stop of a Latin American tour that started in Chile.
